dedupe_keys.name: flexies flexibility from interconnections and electricity storages power system model

description: FLEXIES (Flexibility from Interconnections and Electricity Storages) is a power system optimisation model that investigates which flexibility technologies fully decarbonised power systems need. It was developed at ETH Zurich in a master's thesis by Mattia Maeder supervised by Olga Weiss (2020), and introduced in the Applied Energy paper Assessing the need for flexibility technologies in decarbonized power systems: a new model applied to Central Europe, by Mattia Maeder, Olga Weiss and Konstantinos Boulouchos (2021). The model optimises the use and sizing of interconnections and electricity storage alongside renewable generation, to show how flexibility needs change as fossil plants leave the system. The code is a single MATLAB script with a readme, and the current version is tailored to the Central Europe case study, whose input data set is published as a separate Zenodo record that must be loaded to run the optimisation. Coverage is Central Europe in the provided data. Code and data are downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the code is specific to the Central Europe case, MATLAB is required, and there has been no update since 2021. Simulation uses are capacity planning of storage and interconnections for decarbonised systems. Related records: model-dispa-set and model-urbs are more general open models of European power systems.
